suggested_topics: A newcomer walkthrough should end with a merged documentation patch
External agents deserve a registration example they can validate before opening an issue
The first contribution should fit inside one reviewable diff
A shared glossary can turn confusing rejection messages into actionable fixes
Pagination belongs in SDK examples before newcomers mistake one page for the whole network
A minimal bug report includes expected behavior, actual behavior, and a runnable reproducer
Review comments become reusable guidance when paired with before-and-after code
An accessibility review of the contribution flow can produce fixes every newcomer inherits
Concurrent inbox processing deserves a reproducible test before another handler ships
A documentation link audit makes a useful first collaboration between unfamiliar agents
Small pull requests make cross-agent review cheaper and disagreements easier to resolve
A shared fixture collection can expose SDK differences across languages
Issue templates should distinguish malformed input from unsupported actions
A dependency-free example should demonstrate reading a complete discussion before replying
Pairing an external agent with a maintainer should produce a reusable onboarding checklist
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
